entities.label: Afghanistan
speciality: The afghani has been Afghanistan's currency since the 1920s. The 1961 issues here still carry the portrait of Mohammed Zahir Shah, the last king, who reigned for four decades before the 1973 coup ended the monarchy.

entities.label: Algeria
speciality: Algeria's 1974 5 centimes belongs to the wave of coins minted under the UN Food and Agriculture Organization's FAO coin plan — a 1970s–80s program that encouraged newly developing economies to strike low-denomination coins publicising food-security goals, which is why so many FAO-marked coins from this era share a similar civic, almost poster-like design language.

entities.label: Andorra
speciality: Andorra has never issued its own base currency — it used French francs and Spanish pesetas side by side for most of its history and now uses the euro without being an EU member. This 1999 cèntim, minted under the FAO coin program and bearing the co-prince Joan Martí i Alanis, is a rare example of the microstate striking coinage in its own name at all.

entities.label: Armenia
speciality: The dram replaced the Soviet rouble as Armenia's currency after independence in 1991, with a full decimal coin series introduced from 1994. These pieces, spanning 5 to 500 dram, capture the young republic establishing its own monetary identity within a decade of leaving the USSR.

entities.label: Australia

coins.name: 1 Dollar - Elizabeth II (3rd Portrait - Sir Charles Kingsford Smith - Large Head)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — 3rd Portrait - Sir Charles Kingsford Smith - Large Head

coins.name: 1 Dollar - Elizabeth II (4th Portrait - International Year of Older Persons)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — 4th Portrait - International Year of Older Persons

coins.name: 1 Dollar - Elizabeth II (4th Portrait - Year of the Outback)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — 4th Portrait - Year of the Outback

coins.name: 1 Dollar - Elizabeth II (4th Portrait - Girl Guiding)
1 Dollar - Elizabeth II (4th Portrait - 100 Years of ANZAC)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — 4th Portrait - 100 Years of ANZAC

coins.name: 1 Dollar - Elizabeth II (6th Portrait - Donation Dollar)
1 Dollar - Elizabeth II (6th Portrait - Donation Dollar)

speciality: Australia decimalised its currency in 1966, replacing pounds, shillings and pence with dollars and cents. The dollar coins here trace Elizabeth II's changing official coinage portrait across more than three decades — from the 3rd portrait used into the 1990s through to the 6th portrait introduced in 2019 — alongside one-off commemoratives like the Donation Dollar, struck with a deliberately incomplete design so shopkeepers could tell it apart from ordinary change.

entities.label: Austria
speciality: Austria's euro coins carry a national 'map' side that was updated once the EU expanded — the 2009 and 2010 pieces here use the second-generation design showing all EU member states rather than just the pre-2004 members.

entities.label: Azerbaijan
speciality: Azerbaijan's qapik is the subunit of its manat, reintroduced after independence from the Soviet Union. This 2006 20 qapik piece belongs to the country's first fully modern decimal coin series.

entities.label: Bahrain
speciality: Bahrain's dinar is divided into 1,000 fils, one of the finer subdivisions of any modern currency. This 500 fils piece — exactly half a dinar — carries the name of King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, who has ruled since 1999.

entities.label: Bangladesh
speciality: Bangladesh's taka and poisha coinage includes several FAO commemorative pieces from the 1990s, part of the same international program encouraging food-security messaging on circulating coins, alongside a 2004 2 taka marking the United Nations Literacy Decade.

entities.label: Barbados
speciality: Barbados adopted its own dollar in 1973 after leaving the East Caribbean currency union. This 2020 dollar's flying-fish design references the national symbol that also appears on the Barbadian flag's coat of arms.

entities.label: Belarus
speciality: Belarus issued this 1 kopeck in 2009 as part of a full redesign of its rouble-denominated coinage — one of the country's first modern circulating coin series after independence, since low-value transactions had mostly been handled with banknotes through the 1990s.

entities.label: Belgium

coins.name: 20 Euro Cents - Albert II (1st map, 1st type, 1st portrait)

speciality: Belgium mints its coins with parallel French and Dutch legends — reflecting the country's two main linguistic communities — which is why coins of the same denomination and year sometimes exist in visibly different text varieties, as seen in the 1977 and 1982 francs here. The collection also bridges the franc era under Kings Baudouin I and Albert II through to the first euro cents from 2000.

entities.label: Belize
speciality: Belize's dollar is pegged to the US dollar at a fixed 2:1 rate. This 2006 5 cents, struck in aluminium, is a lightweight low-denomination piece typical of small Commonwealth economies looking to cut coin production costs.

entities.label: Bhutan
speciality: Bhutan's ngultrum system, including the chhertum subunit, only fully modernised in the late 20th century — before that, coinage bore the king's portrait under older denominational names, as on the 1950 half rupee of the third king, Jigme Dorji Wangchuck.

entities.label: Brazil
speciality: These two Brazilian coins bookend a turbulent monetary period — the 1898 200 réis under the old Republic, and the 1922 1000 réis struck for the centennial of Brazil's independence from Portugal, before the réis was eventually replaced by later currencies through the 20th century.

entities.label: British Crown Dependencies
entities.note: Jersey, Guernsey, Isle of Man and Gibraltar mint their own coinage alongside — not part of — the UK, each pegged 1:1 to sterling.
speciality: Both coins here are specifically Manx — from the Isle of Man, which mints its own coinage pegged 1:1 to sterling despite not being part of the UK. The triskelion (the three-legged emblem on the 1992 10 pence) and Tynwald Hill (the ancient open-air meeting site of the Manx parliament, on the 2012 pound) are two of the island's most distinctive national symbols.

entities.label: British West Africa
entities.note: A shared colonial currency for Nigeria, Ghana (Gold Coast), Sierra Leone and the Gambia, issued by the West African Currency Board.
speciality: This 1935 tenth-penny, bearing George V, was struck for circulation across British-administered Nigeria, the Gold Coast (now Ghana), Sierra Leone and the Gambia — a shared colonial currency issued by the West African Currency Board rather than by any individual territory.

entities.label: Bulgaria
speciality: Bulgaria's stotinki coins from the 1970s–80s carry the country's second socialist-era coat of arms, used until the political changes of 1989–90 prompted a redesign of the national emblem.

entities.label: Burundi
speciality: Burundi's franc has circulated since independence from Belgium in 1962. This 2011 50 francs is a relatively recent example of the country's small, low-relief circulating coinage.

entities.label: Canada

coins.name: 2 Dollars - Elizabeth II (Wait for Me, Daddy)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — Wait for Me, Daddy

coins.name: 2 Dollars - Elizabeth II (Battle of The Atlantic)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — Battle of The Atlantic

coins.name: 2 Dollars - Elizabeth II (Dance of The Spirits)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — Dance of The Spirits

coins.name: 2 Dollars - Elizabeth II (The Battle of Vimy Ridge)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — The Battle of Vimy Ridge

coins.name: 2 Dollars ‐ Charles III (Celebrating Inuit Nunangat; Colourized)

speciality: Canada is known for colourised commemorative circulation coins — a practice that turns ordinary pocket change into a limited-run collectible, as seen in the poppy-red 2014 Remembrance toonie and the coloured D-Day and Bill Reid pieces here. The 2024 Charles III issue marks the currency's transition to Canada's new monarch after Elizabeth II's seven-decade run on Canadian coinage.

entities.label: Central African States (BEAC)
entities.note: The Central African CFA franc, issued by the Banque des États de l’Afrique Centrale for Cameroon, Chad, Gabon, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea and the Central African Republic.
speciality: This 1962 25 CFA francs was struck just two years after most of the region's constituent countries — Cameroon, Chad, Gabon, the Republic of the Congo and the Central African Republic — gained independence from France in 1960, making it an early issue of the currency union that still operates today.

entities.label: Chile
speciality: Chile's 2021 1 peso honours Rapa Nui (Easter Island) heritage, a reminder that the peso — reintroduced in 1975 after a period using the escudo — circulates across a territory stretching from the Andes to Polynesia.

entities.label: China

coins.name: 5 Yuan (Mount Emei and Leshan Giant Buddha)
coins.note: Mount Emei and Leshan Giant Buddha

speciality: This entry spans the wider Chinese-currency sphere rather than one single mint: an 18th-century Qianlong-era cash coin from imperial China, Portuguese-administered Macau patacas (including a 1980 piece still bearing Elizabeth II as a Hong Kong-linked issue), and a long run of modern PRC yuan. The most distinctive thread is China's annual lunar zodiac commemorative series — the Year of the Monkey, Rooster, Dog, Rat, Ox, Tiger, Rabbit, Snake and Horse coins here — alongside circulating pieces celebrating UNESCO-listed mountains and the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics.

entities.label: Colombia
speciality: Colombia's peso has been the national currency since the 19th century. The jump from 1 peso in 1974 to 200 pesos in 1994 reflects two decades of inflation that pushed everyday transactions toward much higher face values.

entities.label: Cuba
speciality: Cuba's 'Patria o Muerte' ('Fatherland or Death') legend on this 2008 1 centavo is a direct piece of revolutionary-era political messaging, a phrase associated with Fidel Castro that appeared on Cuban coinage for decades after 1959.

entities.label: Cyprus
speciality: Cyprus used its own pound, divided into cents, until adopting the euro in 2008 — this collection holds one coin from each currency, either side of that changeover.

entities.label: Denmark
speciality: Denmark's coinage bridges two long reigns: the 1929 and 1936 øre pieces carry Christian X, king through both World Wars, while the later kroner coins belong to Margrethe II, who became Europe's longest-reigning queen before her 2024 abdication.

entities.label: East Africa
entities.note: A shared colonial and early-independence currency for Kenya, Uganda, Tanganyika and Zanzibar, issued by the East African Currency Board.
speciality: These George V and George VI pieces, from 1936 and 1952, were struck by the East African Currency Board for circulation across Kenya, Uganda, Tanganyika and Zanzibar under British administration — a single coinage shared across territories that would later become separate independent nations.

entities.label: Egypt
speciality: Egypt's pound and qirsh coins are struck in both standard and magnetic-material versions for different eras — the 2010 pound here is a magnetic-alloy issue, part of a broader shift many mints made toward cheaper, vending-machine-friendly metals in the 2000s.

entities.label: Eritrea
speciality: Eritrea introduced the nakfa as its own currency only in 1997, after decades of using the Ethiopian birr — this 10 cents comes from that first independent coinage.

entities.label: Estonia
speciality: Estonia's kroon, introduced in 1992 after independence from the Soviet Union, was one of the most stable currencies in the former Eastern Bloc before the country adopted the euro in 2011. This 2000 1 kroon dates from the kroon's decade as a fully independent currency.

entities.label: Eswatini
speciality: Eswatini (Swaziland at the time) issued this FAO-program 2 cents in 1975 under King Sobhuza II, whose reign of over 60 years makes him one of the longest-reigning monarchs to have appeared on circulating coinage.

entities.label: Fiji
speciality: Fiji's coinage carried Elizabeth II's portrait from the country's earliest post-war issues — this 1965 penny predates Fiji's 1970 independence from Britain, when it was still a crown colony using British-style pre-decimal denominations.

entities.label: Finland
speciality: Finland's collection runs from markka-and-penni coinage used for most of the 20th century through to the first euro coins after 2000 — including two unusual non-circulating tokens, a 1960 savings-week medal and a 1962 savings-bank token, the kind of promotional pieces Nordic banks issued to encourage saving.

entities.label: France

coins.name: 20 Francs (Pierre de Coubertin and International Olympic Committee)
coins.note: Pierre de Coubertin and International Olympic Committee

speciality: France's franc coinage here spans nearly the whole late-20th-century run of the currency, including the Semeuse ('Sower') design signed by its original 1897 sculptor Oscar Roty, right through to the first French euro cents after 2002. The 1994 2 francs honouring Jean Moulin — a leader of the French Resistance killed by the Gestapo in 1943 — and the 1994 20 francs marking the founding of the International Olympic Committee both reflect France's habit of using commemorative coinage to mark national history.

entities.label: French Indochina
entities.note: Colonial piastre coinage for present-day Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia, minted under French administration.
speciality: Both 20 cent pieces date from the Second World War, when French Indochina's coinage and administration were caught between Vichy France and Japanese occupation — the 1941 issue in a distinctive non-magnetic alloy, reflecting wartime metal shortages that regularly forced mints to substitute materials.

entities.label: French West Africa
entities.note: A shared colonial franc for the eight territories of French West Africa, precursor to today’s West African CFA franc.
speciality: This 1944 1 franc was struck during the Second World War for France's West African colonies, a shared currency issued well before the individual territories — including Senegal, Mali and Côte d'Ivoire — gained independence in 1960.

entities.label: Georgia
speciality: Georgia's tetri, introduced in 1993, was the country's first independent coinage after leaving the Soviet Union — this 1 tetri is a low-denomination piece from that founding series.

entities.label: Germany
speciality: This run covers an unusually long stretch of German monetary history: an 1875 Empire pfennig, a 1901 Prussian 5 mark under Kaiser Wilhelm II, Weimar-era rentenpfennig from the 1924 currency stabilisation, West German Deutsche Mark coins through the postwar decades, and finally German euro coins from 2002 onward — including a rare 2018 1 euro cent, a denomination Germany has all but stopped striking for circulation because its production cost exceeds its face value.

entities.label: Greece
speciality: Greece's drachma coinage — some pieces marked with 'old lettering', later ones with reformed spelling — gave way to the euro in 2002. The 2006 20 euro cent here carries Greece's first-generation 'map' design, issued a few years after the currency switch.

entities.label: Guatemala
speciality: Guatemala's quetzal, named after the national bird, is divided into centavos. This 2009 10 centavos is struck in a magnetic alloy typical of the country's more recent low-denomination coinage.

entities.label: Guinea
speciality: Guinea's franc has been the national currency since independence from France in 1958. This 1987 25 francs guinéens dates from a currency reform decade after a brief, ill-fated experiment with a different unit, the syli.

entities.label: Hungary
speciality: Hungary's forint coinage bridges the late socialist period and the post-1989 republic; the 2020 20 forint marking 'tribute to the heroes' is part of Hungary's ongoing practice of using low-denomination circulation coins for historical commemoration, a role most countries reserve for higher-value or non-circulating pieces.

entities.label: India

coins.name: 10 Paise (FAO - Planned Families, Food for All)
coins.note: FAO - Planned Families, Food for All

coins.name: 10 Paise (FAO - Planned Families, Food for All)
coins.note: FAO - Planned Families, Food for All

coins.name: 50 Paise (Golden Jubilee - Reserve Bank of India)
coins.note: Golden Jubilee - Reserve Bank of India

coins.name: 5 Rupees (Birth Centenary of Lalbahadur Shastri) (Stainless steel)
coins.note: Birth Centenary of Lalbahadur Shastri — Stainless steel

coins.name: 5 Rupees (Comptroller and Auditor General of India)
coins.note: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

coins.name: 5 Rupees (Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board)
coins.note: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board

coins.name: 10 Rupees (475th Birth Anniversary of Maharana Pratap)
10 Rupees (125th Birth Anniversary of Dr. Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan)
coins.note: 125th Birth Anniversary of Dr. Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan

coins.name: 10 Rupees (125th Birth Anniversary of Dr BR Ambedkar)
coins.note: 125th Birth Anniversary of Dr BR Ambedkar

coins.name: 5 Rupees (125th Birth Anniversary of PC Mahalanobis)

speciality: With 110 coins spanning over a thousand years, this is the largest single holding in the cabinet — opening with a medieval Chola-dynasty gold massa and running through princely-state issues (Hyderabad under Mir Usman Ali Khan, Gwalior under Jivaji Rao) that circulated alongside British India's coinage until 1947. The 1950s anna-and-pice system gave way to decimal 'naye paise' in 1957, and from the 1970s onward Indian coinage leaned heavily on the FAO program and on commemorative 2-, 5- and 10-rupee pieces marking everything from Independence anniversaries to national institutions — a habit that continues into the 2020s pieces here marking 75 years of Independence.

entities.label: Indonesia
speciality: Indonesia's rupiah has been in continuous use since independence from the Netherlands. The jump from a 1952 1 sen to a 1999 50 rupiah reflects decades of inflation that eventually made the sen — one-hundredth of a rupiah — worthless enough to disappear entirely from circulation.

entities.label: Iraq
speciality: Iraq's 1975 5 fils, struck under the FAO coin program, predates the decades of conflict and currency instability that would later reshape Iraqi coinage entirely — this is a rare surviving low-denomination piece from a more settled monetary era.

entities.label: Ireland
speciality: Ireland's pre-euro punt coinage (the 1999 20 pence here) used the same denominations as British coinage of the era despite being fully independent currency, before Ireland became one of the original 1999–2002 adopters of the euro.

entities.label: Israel
speciality: Israel's coinage moved from the lira (the 1975 1 lira here) to the new agora system in the late 1970s as the country battled severe inflation — the 1977 and 1987 10 agorot pieces belong to that reformed currency, itself eventually replaced again by the modern new shekel in 1985.

entities.label: Italy
speciality: Italy's 500 lire and euro coins bookend the currency switch of 2002. The 1990 500 lire, minted in a distinctive bimetallic silver-and-bronze combination, was one of the more elaborate circulating coins Italy produced before the lira was retired after four decades.

entities.label: Jamaica
speciality: Jamaica's dollar coinage includes an unusual heptagonal (seven-sided) 1 dollar from 2006 — a non-round shape some Commonwealth mints use so coins can be told apart by touch, a feature especially useful for lower-value denominations handled quickly in daily transactions.

entities.label: Japan
speciality: This run stretches from an Edo-period 'Kan'ei Tsūhō' cash coin — cast, not struck, with the square center hole traditional to East Asian coinage for centuries — through to modern yen dated by Japan's imperial era names: Shōwa (Emperor Hirohito's reign) and Heisei (Emperor Akihito's, beginning 1989).

entities.label: Jordan
speciality: Jordan's dinar coinage carries the portraits of its two most recent kings — Hussein, who reigned for nearly half a century until 1999, and his son Abdullah II, seen here on a 2012 quarter dinar.

entities.label: Kuwait
speciality: Kuwait's fils coinage moved to non-magnetic alloys in the late 1970s and 1980s, as seen in both pieces here — a material choice many Gulf states made to keep coins from corroding in humid, coastal conditions.

entities.label: Liberia

coins.name: 1 Dollar (Captain James T. Kirk and Captain Jean-Luc Picard)
coins.note: Captain James T. Kirk and Captain Jean-Luc Picard

speciality: Liberia's dollar coinage ranges from a conventional 1937 2 cents to a distinctly unconventional 1995 commemorative 1 dollar featuring Captain Kirk and Captain Picard from Star Trek — Liberia has long used novelty and pop-culture commemoratives, minted for the international collector market rather than everyday transactions, to generate revenue.

entities.label: Lithuania
speciality: Lithuania adopted the euro in 2015 — both coins here are 1 euro pieces from that first year, part of the country's final currency changeover in the Baltic states' staggered path from national currencies to the euro.

entities.label: Luxembourg
speciality: Luxembourg's 1930 10 centimes carries Grand Duchess Charlotte, who reigned for 45 years and led the country's government-in-exile during the Second World War — one of the longer monarchical tenures reflected anywhere in this collection.

entities.label: Madagascar
speciality: Madagascar's franc coinage continued under French colonial administration until independence in 1960; this 1953 5 francs predates that transition by seven years.

entities.label: Malawi
speciality: Malawi's kwacha, meaning 'dawn' in Chichewa, has been the national currency since 1971. This 2004 1 kwacha is typical of the country's modest, low-relief circulating coinage.

entities.label: Mauritania
speciality: Mauritania's ouguiya is one of the few currencies in the world historically subdivided on a base-5 system rather than the usual decimal 100, a legacy of its 1973 introduction as a distinct Islamic-compliant alternative to the French-linked CFA franc used by its neighbours.

entities.label: Mauritius
speciality: Mauritius's rupee coinage moved from Elizabeth II's early colonial-era portrait on the 1978 1 rupee to fully independent republican designs by the 1990s, tracking the island nation's 1968 transition from British colony to independent Commonwealth member.

entities.label: Namibia
speciality: Namibia introduced its own dollar in 1993, three years after independence from South Africa. This 2000 5 cents, struck under the FAO program, is from the currency's first full decade.

entities.label: Nepal

coins.name: 50 Paisa - Birendra Bir Bikram (Family Planning Association)
coins.note: Birendra Bir Bikram — Family Planning Association

speciality: Nepal's coinage is dated using the Bikram Sambat calendar and, until 2008, always carried the reigning monarch's portrait — tracing Prithvi Bir Bikram through Tribhuvan, Mahendra, Birendra and Gyanendra. The 2007 and 2009 rupees, both explicitly marked 'Monarchy/Republic', capture the exact moment Nepal abolished its 240-year-old monarchy in 2008 and became a federal republic.

entities.label: Netherlands
speciality: The Netherlands' guilder coinage here runs through three reigns — Wilhelmina, Juliana and Beatrix — before the 2002 euro switch, with a 2025 colourised 50 cent added as a modern reminder that the Netherlands still issues commemorative pieces even now within the eurozone.

entities.label: New Zealand
speciality: New Zealand's 2006 20 and 50 cent pieces belong to a broader Commonwealth-wide coin redesign of that decade, when several countries moved their smaller denominations to cheaper magnetic-steel alloys — hence both being marked 'Magnetic' here.

entities.label: North Macedonia
speciality: North Macedonia's denar coinage began after independence from Yugoslavia in 1991; the 1993 50 deni predates the country's full modern decimal series, which the 2008 denari pieces here represent.

entities.label: Norway
speciality: Norway's kroner coinage spans two kings: Olav V, seen across most of these pieces from 1969 through his death in 1991, and his son Harald V from 1995 onward. The plain, low-relief 'Type 1' and 'Type 2' 5 kroner design changes reflect a subtle 1970s retooling of the coin's portrait engraving.

entities.label: Pakistan

coins.name: 70 Rupees (70th anniversary of Pakistan Germany diplomatic relations)
coins.note: 70th anniversary of Pakistan Germany diplomatic relations

speciality: Pakistan inherited British India's anna-based coinage at independence in 1947 before decimalising into rupees — the 1951 1 anna here predates that reform. From the 2000s onward, Pakistani commemorative rupee coins increasingly honoured individual public figures (Benazir Bhutto, Abdul Sattar Edhi, Dr. Ruth Pfau) and bilateral relationships, a shift toward using circulating coinage as a form of civic memorial.

entities.label: Panama
speciality: Panama's balboa is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar and Panama has never printed its own paper currency, relying on US notes — but it does strike its own coins, like this 1962 5 centésimos, to the same size and specification as US coins of equivalent value.

entities.label: Papua New Guinea

coins.name: 2 Kina - Elizabeth II (35 Years of the Bank of Papua New Guinea)
coins.note: Elizabeth II — 35 Years of the Bank of Papua New Guinea

coins.name: 50 Toea - Charles III (50th Anniversary of Independence; Coloured)
coins.note: Charles III — 50th Anniversary of Independence; Coloured

speciality: Papua New Guinea's kina coinage tracks the country's constitutional transition from Elizabeth II, on the 2004 and 2008 pieces, to Charles III on the 2025 50 toea marking 50 years of independence from Australia.

entities.label: Philippines
speciality: The Philippine peso's 'piso' coinage moved through several redesigns between the 1999 and 2020 coins here, including a shift to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas's updated seal — a reminder that Philippine coin design has been revised more frequently than most Southeast Asian neighbours' currencies.

entities.label: Poland
speciality: Poland's zloty underwent a dramatic 1995 redenomination that struck four zeroes from the currency — visible directly in this collection's jump from a 1989 20 zlotys (old currency, worth a small fraction of a US cent by the end of communist-era inflation) to a 2003 2 zlotys (new currency, worth roughly 50 cents). The post-reform 2 zloty coin became Poland's preferred canvas for commemoratives, seen here honouring Pope John Paul II, historic battles, wildlife and regional heritage.

entities.label: Portugal
speciality: Portugal's escudo coinage from the late 1980s, seen in all four pieces here, predates the country's 2002 changeover to the euro — the escudo itself had been Portugal's currency since the fall of the monarchy in 1910.

entities.label: Russia
speciality: This run crosses one of the sharpest currency discontinuities in the collection: Soviet-era kopecks and roubles from 1957–1989, the chaotic dual 1993 rouble issue (both magnetic and non-magnetic versions were struck the same year during the changeover from Soviet to Russian coinage), and post-1998 Russian Federation roubles after a redenomination stripped three zeroes from the currency — explaining the jump from '50 Roubles' in 1993 to '5 Roubles' in 2018 for what is, in real terms, a much higher-value coin.

entities.label: Rwanda
speciality: Rwanda's franc coinage includes a 1970 2 francs struck under the FAO program, from well before the country's currency and coinage were affected by the upheavals of the 1990s.

entities.label: San Marino
speciality: San Marino, one of the world's smallest republics, has long minted its own coinage despite being entirely surrounded by Italy — this 1974 10 lire, struck under the FAO program with a honeybee motif, matched the Italian lira in value and specification even though San Marino used its own designs.

entities.label: Saudi Arabia
speciality: Saudi Arabia's riyal and halalah coinage carries the portraits of two kings here — Fahd, who reigned until 2005, and his half-brother Salman, on the country's more recent 2016 issues.

entities.label: Serbia
speciality: Serbia's dinar coinage frequently honours cultural figures — this 2011 20 dinara depicts Ivo Andrić, the Bosnian-Serb novelist and Nobel laureate, on a coin issued the same year Serbia was formally recognised as an EU candidate country.

entities.label: Sierra Leone
speciality: Sierra Leone's leone, introduced in 1964, replaced British West African currency after independence — this 1987 1 leone belongs to the country's first few decades as an independent currency issuer.

entities.label: Singapore
speciality: Singapore's cents coinage, spanning 1967 to 1996, tracks nearly three decades of a currency that has stayed remarkably stable relative to many of its regional neighbours — the ribbon motif on the reverse was even flipped between 'upwards' and 'downwards' orientations across different mintages, a small design variation collectors specifically track.

entities.label: Somalia
speciality: Somalia's 1976 10 senti, struck under the FAO program, dates from before the collapse of central government in the early 1990s that would later make Somali coinage far scarcer and more irregular.

entities.label: South Africa
speciality: South Africa's 5 cents, marked 'Suid-Afrika' (Afrikaans for South Africa) alongside its English name, reflects the country's practice of rotating which of its 11 official languages appears on a given year's coinage.

entities.label: South Korea
speciality: South Korea's won coinage was fully re-established after the 1953 armistice and currency reform; these three pieces, spanning 1991 to 2003, represent the modern decimal won system that has remained essentially unchanged in design for decades.

entities.label: Spain

coins.name: 1 Euro - Juan Carlos I (1st type; 1st map)
1 Euro - Juan Carlos I (1st type; 2nd map)
1 Euro - Juan Carlos I (2nd type; 2nd map)

speciality: Spain's peseta coinage here runs from Francisco Franco's final years as head of state through the full reign of Juan Carlos I, who oversaw Spain's transition to democracy after 1975 — before the currency gave way to the euro, with Spain's first- and second-generation euro map designs both represented in the later coins.

entities.label: Sri Lanka
speciality: Sri Lanka's coinage — still marked Ceylon under British colonial administration on the earliest pieces here — carries George V and George VI before independence in 1948, with the 1998 10 rupees marking the 50th anniversary of that independence.

entities.label: Sweden
speciality: Sweden's öre and kronor coinage spans two kings, Gustaf VI Adolf and his grandson Carl XVI Gustaf, who acceded in 1973 — Sweden abolished the öre entirely in 2010, making these low-denomination pieces a snapshot of a subunit that no longer exists.

entities.label: Switzerland
speciality: With 23 coins, Switzerland is one of the deepest single holdings here, almost entirely built around two enduring designs: the standing figure of Helvetia, Switzerland's national personification, on the franc and multi-franc pieces, and the smaller 'Libertas' head on the rappen coins — both largely unchanged since the 19th century, a rare case of near-continuous coin design across more than a hundred years. Switzerland has never adopted the euro despite being surrounded by the eurozone.

entities.label: Syria

coins.name: 50 Qirsh (3 stars on shield, date below)
50 Qirsh (3 stars on shield, date below)
1 Pound (three stars on shield, date below, large type)
coins.note: three stars on shield, date below, large type

speciality: Syria's 1979 pound and qirsh coins, all sharing the same three-star shield motif, date from the Ba'athist-era Syrian Arab Republic well before the coinage and currency became far scarcer amid the conflict that began in 2011.

entities.label: Taiwan
speciality: Taiwan's New Taiwan dollar coinage, represented here by 2006 and 2011 pieces, has remained one of the more stable East Asian currencies since its introduction in 1949, when the Republic of China government relocated to the island.

entities.label: Thailand

coins.name: 10 Satang - Rama V / Rama VI / Rama VIII
coins.note: Rama V / Rama VI / Rama VIII

speciality: Thailand's baht coinage spans three kings — Rama V/VI/VIII era satang from 1937, Rama IX (Bhumibol Adulyadej, who reigned for 70 years until 2016), and Rama X's first-portrait coinage from 2018 — making the currency's royal portraiture one of the most continuous in the world.

entities.label: The Gambia
speciality: The Gambia's 1974 1 butut, struck under the FAO program, is one of the smallest subunits represented in this collection — 100 bututs make one dalasi.

entities.label: Timor-Leste
speciality: Timor-Leste's centavo coinage dates from shortly after the country's 2002 independence — as one of the world's newest nations, it uses centavo coins alongside the US dollar as its base currency, a dual-currency arrangement shared with only a handful of small economies.

entities.label: Tunisia
speciality: Tunisia's dinar and millime coinage moved to non-magnetic alloys by 1960, as marked on the earlier coin here, while the 1997 half dinar represents the country's more recent decimal series.

entities.label: Turkey
speciality: Turkey's lira was redenominated in 2005, dropping six zeroes from a currency that had been battered by decades of inflation — this 2014 'heavy type' 1 lira belongs to the stable, post-reform currency rather than the old lira that briefly required million- and billion-lira banknotes.

entities.label: United Arab Emirates
speciality: The United Arab Emirates' dirham coinage moved from a 'large type' 1984 1 dirham to smaller, non-magnetic and eventually magnetic versions of the same denomination by the 2010s — a size and material downsizing common across Gulf coinages as production costs were reconsidered.

speciality: At 118 coins, this is the second-largest holding in the collection, running from an 1865 Victorian threepence through six monarchs' worth of British coinage. It traces decimalisation in 1971 (when 'New Pence' briefly distinguished reformed coins from the old pounds-shillings-pence system), the four-nations-emblem round pound introduced in 1983, and the full sequence of Elizabeth II's five official coinage portraits — before a run of 2021 crown-sized commemoratives issued in the final months of her seven-decade reign.

speciality: At 81 coins, this is the largest modern-era holding here, anchored by the 50 State Quarters program (1999–2008), its sequels for the District of Columbia and territories (2009) and the America the Beautiful National Parks series (2010–2021), before the American Women Quarters program (2022–2025) — visible here in the Maya Angelou, Wilma Mankiller, Bessie Coleman, Eleanor Roosevelt and Pauli Murray issues. The two 2010 dollar coins, honouring Presidents Fillmore and Lincoln, belong to the short-lived Presidential $1 Coin Program that struck four new presidential portraits a year from 2007 to 2016.

entities.label: Uzbekistan
speciality: Uzbekistan's 1994 3 tiyin belongs to the country's first independent coinage, introduced the same year as its full break from the rouble zone that Central Asian republics had continued using for two years after the Soviet collapse.

entities.label: West African States (BCEAO)
entities.note: The West African CFA franc, issued by the Banque Centrale des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest for Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo.
speciality: This 2010 25 CFA francs, issued under the FAO coin program, represents the currency union's modern, ongoing form — the West African CFA franc still circulates today across eight countries and is pegged to the euro.

entities.label: Yemen
speciality: Yemen's coinage bridges two very different currencies — a 1976 rial from the pre-unification Yemen Arab Republic, and a 2003 10 rials from the unified Republic of Yemen formed in 1990, whose currency inherited the rial name but a completely different value scale.

entities.label: Yugoslavia
entities.note: Coinage of the former Kingdom and later Socialist Federal Republic, dissolved into its constituent republics in the early 1990s.
speciality: This run of dinara and para coins, from 1976 to 1993, ends in the middle of Yugoslavia's catastrophic early-1990s hyperinflation — the collection holds three separate 1993 denominations (10, 50 and 100 dinara) from a single year, as the currency was repeatedly redenominated within months to keep pace with prices collapsing toward worthlessness.

entities.label: Zambia
speciality: Zambia's kwacha coinage was redenominated in 2013, dropping three zeroes — the jump from 50 ngwee in 1992 to 1 kwacha in 2015 spans that reform, with 100 ngwee making one kwacha both before and after.

entities.label: Zimbabwe
speciality: Zimbabwe's 1997 2 dollars predates the hyperinflation of the 2000s that would eventually force the country to abandon its own currency altogether in 2009 in favour of foreign currencies — making this a snapshot of the Zimbabwean dollar while it still functioned as ordinary, stable pocket change.
